subject: physics
title: Energy Stored in a Capacitor
welcome_lead: Integrate Q V to find the energy locked in a charged capacitor.
meta_desc: A-Level Capacitance adventure on energy stored as ½CV² and ½QV.
final_note: Half the work goes to the capacitor, half to resistive losses when charging from a battery.

concepts.def: Same energy, using C and V.
Same energy, using Q and C.
Area under Q vs V triangle.
50% of battery energy wasted in charging R.

walkthroughs.body_html: As charge builds, voltage rises linearly from 0 to V. Total energy is the area under the line, which is ½ × Q × V — a triangle.
E = ½ Q V = ½ C V² = Q² / (2C). Use whichever pair you know. Doubling V quadruples stored energy.
Battery delivers QV of energy when charging. Half ends up as ½ Q V on the capacitor; the other half is dissipated in resistance, regardless of R value.
